Where it began

Kamran Akmal was born in Lahore on 13 January 1982 and went to school at the Beaconhouse School System. He grew up in a big household, the fourth of seven brothers with one sister, and cricket ran right through it.

Two of his younger brothers, Adnan and Umar, also became professional cricketers, Adnan as a wicketkeeper like Kamran and Umar as a batsman who could take the gloves when needed. Babar Azam, who went on to captain Pakistan, is his first cousin.

The player

His Test career began at Harare Sports Club in November 2002. He played 53 Tests for Pakistan up to 2010, making 2,648 runs at 30.79 with six hundreds, twelve fifties and a best of 158 not out. Behind the stumps he took 184 catches and made 22 stumpings.

His first Test hundred was one that mattered. Coming in at number eight at Mohali, with Pakistan only 39 ahead of India, he made 109 and saved the match. On another day, with Pakistan 39 for 6, he hit a century that lifted the total to 245 and helped win both the game and the series. Early in 2006 he made seven international hundreds in the space of six months.

What made him special

He liked to score fast from wherever he was sent in, and in one-day cricket he was happy to open, once making hundreds in consecutive matches against England. Keeping wicket is the most unforgiving job on the field, and his glovework had its quieter days, but his hands could be lightning quick. At the 2009 World Twenty20, which Pakistan won, he stumped four Netherlands batsmen in one match, a world record.

The runs kept coming at home, too. Nobody made more runs than his 1,035 in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy of 2016–17; he shared an unbeaten opening stand of 209 that set a world record in T20 cricket, and in 2020 he became the first wicketkeeper to reach 100 stumpings in the format.

Away from the middle

He was part of the Rajasthan Royals side that won the first IPL in 2008, and he was a Peshawar Zalmi player from the first PSL season in 2016 to his last in 2022. In 2017 his hundred off 60 balls against Karachi Kings took Zalmi into the final, which they won; he finished as the leading run-scorer with 353 and collected the awards for the best batsman and the best wicketkeeper of the season. He made three PSL hundreds in all.

He retired in February 2023 and moved straight into coaching and selection, becoming batting mentor at Peshawar Zalmi and helping choose the under-13, under-16 and under-19 regional sides.

And finally

With two brothers in the game and a cousin who captained his country, arguments at family gatherings about who was the best batsman at the table must have been hard to settle. Kamran could always point out that he was the one with the gloves.
